name.text: 16.1 Q1 Sorting Kenyan relations into function or not a function

questiontext.text:
A tea buying centre in Kericho keeps two sets of records, shown in the arrow diagrams below.

Records 1 link {@farmers@} tea farmers to the two buying centres, {@c1@} and {@c2@}, where they deliver their green leaf. A farmer may deliver to more than one centre.

Records 2 link one national identity card number to two different farmer profiles, because of a mistake in the records.

[[jsxgraph width="400px" height="260px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-6, 5, 6, -2.8], axis: false, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false}); var n = {#farmers#}; b.create('text', [-5.7, 4.4, 'Records 1'], {fontSize: 13, fixed: true}); b.create('text', [1.0, 4.4, 'Records 2'], {fontSize: 13, fixed: true}); // Records 1: farmer i delivers to centre (i odd: top, i even: bottom); farmer k also delivers to the other centre var k = {#k#}; var cx = -1.6, cy = [2.6, -0.6], cname = [{#c1#}, {#c2#}]; for (var j = 0; j < 2; j++) { b.create('point', [cx, cy[j]], {name: cname[j], size: 3, fixed: true, color: '#2e7d32', label: {offset: [-25, j === 0 ? 16 : -16]}}); } for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) { var y = 3.2 - i * 4.4 / (n - 1); var c = (i % 2 === 0) ? 0 : 1; b.create('point', [-4.6, y], {name: 'F' + (i + 1), size: 2, fixed: true, color: '#1565c0', label: {offset: [-22, 0]}}); b.create('arrow', [[-4.4, y], [cx - 0.2, cy[c]]], {strokeColor: '#888888', fixed: true, lastArrow: {size: 5}}); if (i + 1 === k) { b.create('arrow', [[-4.4, y], [cx - 0.2, cy[1 - c]]], {strokeColor: '#888888', fixed: true, lastArrow: {size: 5}}); } } // Records 2: one identity number with two arrows b.create('point', [1.8, 1], {name: 'ID', size: 3, fixed: true, color: '#c62828', label: {offset: [-20, 0]}}); b.create('point', [4.6, 2.6], {name: 'Profile X', size: 2, fixed: true, color: '#1565c0', label: {offset: [-20, 14]}}); b.create('point', [4.6, -0.6], {name: 'Profile Y', size: 2, fixed: true, color: '#1565c0', label: {offset: [-20, -14]}}); b.create('arrow', [[2.0, 1.1], [4.4, 2.5]], {strokeColor: '#c62828', fixed: true, lastArrow: {size: 5}}); b.create('arrow', [[2.0, 0.9], [4.4, -0.5]], {strokeColor: '#c62828', fixed: true, lastArrow: {size: 5}}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

(a) Is Records 1, from farmers to the buying centres, a function?

Records 1 is [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Is Records 2, from the identity number to the profiles, a function?

Records 2 is [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
A relation is a function when every input is linked to exactly one output. Several inputs may share an output; what is not allowed is one input with two or more outputs. So the test is to look at each input in turn and count the arrows leaving it.

(a) In Records 1, farmer F{#k#} delivers to both {@c1@} and {@c2@}, so that one input has two outputs. {@c1@} also receives leaf from several farmers, so an output is shared too. Inputs can have many outputs and outputs can have many inputs: the relation is many-to-many. Because at least one input has more than one output, Records 1 is not a function.

(b) In Records 2, one identity number is linked to two different profiles. That single input has two outputs, so the relation is one-to-many. Records 2 is not a function.

questionnote.text: farmers={@farmers@}, F{#k#} to both centres, centres {@c1@} and {@c2@}; Records 1 many-to-many (not a function), Records 2 one-to-many (not a function).

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the definitions of one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many relations in Section 16.1 (Types of Relations) of the Grade 11 Functions topic.

node.description: Records 1 classified as not a function?

falsefeedback.text: Count the arrows leaving each farmer, not the arrows arriving at each centre. A relation is a function only if every input has exactly one output. Is there a farmer who delivers to more than one centre?

node.description: Records 2 classified as not a function?

falsefeedback.text: Look at the arrows leaving the identity number. A function needs each input to have exactly one output, not just at least one. Count how many outputs that single input has.
